messages.subject: Variance for Hexp
messages.body_plain:
Hi poppr team,
Is there a way to obtain the variance of the Hexp in poppr? Could this be added into the R package?
Cheers Kat
messages.body_snippet:

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Variance for Hexp
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kat,

We didn’t add the variance explicitly in poppr and I’m not exactly sure why, because the calculation seems to be fairly straighforward from Nei and Roychaudhury 1974 (http://www.genetics.org/content/genetics/76/2/379.full.pdf), but does get a bit hairy in Nei 1978 (http://www.genetics.org/content/genetics/89/3/583.full.pdf):

Nevertheless, I think I may have a solution for you from the 1974 pub:

The variance is calculated much as you would expect by taking the square residuals and dividing those by the number of loci minus one. Here’s how I would obtain it with the nancycats data set
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library('poppr'))
data(nancycats)
n <- nLoc(nancycats)
o <- summary(nancycats)$Hobs                # observed heterozygosity
e <- locus_table(nancycats)[seq(n), "Hexp"] # expected heterozygosity
#>
#> allele = Number of observed alleles
#> 1-D = Simpson index
#> Hexp = Nei's 1978 gene diversity
#> ------------------------------------------
print(v <- ((o - e)^2)/(n - 1))             # per-locus variance
#>         fca8        fca23        fca43        fca45        fca77
#> 0.0049759764 0.0020443113 0.0017313233 0.0003610015 0.0071512483
#>        fca78        fca90        fca96        fca37
#> 0.0019382048 0.0035164070 0.0025775979 0.0030448688
mean(v)                                     # overall variance
#> [1] 0.003037882

Regarding adding this into poppr: I don’t have the bandwith to add the code myself (which includes testing and documentation), but I would be happy to review a pull request from anyone who feels up to the challenge.

Hope that helps!

Zhian

messages.subject: mixed-ploidy SNP data (diploids, triploids, and tetraploids)
messages.subject_clean: mixed-ploidy SNP data (diploids, triploids, and tetraploids)
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I'm interested in using poppr for my data, as I have both diploid sexuals and polyploid asexuals and poppr seems like a great option for dealing complicated systems like mine! I'm running into a bit of trouble converting my vcf's for use with poppr and adegenet, particularly in my polyploids (triploids and tetraploids). I have GBS data (technically ddRAD) and a large number of SNPs, so my understanding is that I should be using genlight/snpclone objects. Unfortunately, it seems that genlight cannot handle loci with more than two alleles, so a decent portion of my SNPs are discarded when using vcfR2genlight. Is there any way around this?

Thanks,

Evan Hersh

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] mixed-ploidy SNP data (diploids, triploids, and tetraploids)
messages.subject_clean: [poppr] mixed-ploidy SNP data (diploids, triploids, and tetraploids)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Evan,

I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but I think you are going to have to use "genind" objects for this (using vcfR2genind). The good news is that you can do more things with genind objects than you can with genlight objects, it just takes ~16x more space and some of the distance calculations will be slower. I believe one of the things you might be able to do is to use PCA to find the loci that are most influential for your analyses and subset your data to those loci. I can't recall off the top of my head what the procedure is, but I know it's been discussed in the adegenet forum, which you can search the archives here: http://adegenet.r-forge.r-project.org/search.html

Hope that helps,
Zhian

I am new to R and learning "poppr" and "adegenet" in R package for my data analysis. While performing the following codes/commands for DAPC analysis for my data set, I came across this error message. My data set is haploid and consisting of dominant markers. Since I could not rectify the error with my data set, herewith I attached a sub-sample of my data set for your reference.

I would be grateful to you if you could help me to figure out the error and perform my analysis.

Thank you.

Sincerely,
Buddhika

library("adegenet")
genrr1 <- read.genalex("C:/Users/u1107303/Desktop/genrr1.csv")
splitStrata(genrr1) <- ~location/form
genrr1

dapc.genrr1 <- dapc(genrr1, var.contrib = TRUE, scale = FALSE, n.pca = 30, n.da = nPop(genrr1) - 1)
